editorial.headline: Private Archiving: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Private archiving is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today under the island-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register private archiving in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign ownership of up to 100%. In Bali, every scope at the large-business scale is classified as Low or Medium-Low risk, placing the activity within the province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for those risk classes. The distinction matters: national openness does not overcome the Bali-specific block.

This is a broad information-stewardship activity rather than a narrow document-storage service. It covers archival services undertaken by non-government individuals, organisations, companies, foundations and other private institutions to build, store and classify physical or digital archive collections, then make them accessible to the public or defined groups of users. The work may serve the general public or specific users such as students, researchers, staff or members, and includes the operation of archives themselves.

Its scope reaches across the life of an archive. That includes acquiring or collecting material; identifying, inventorying, describing and classifying it; and maintaining collections through sanitation and climate-condition monitoring, security and safety measures, and rehabilitation. It also includes communicating archives on site or remotely, alongside cultural and educational activities connected to their wider use and appreciation. Archiving paper or electronic documents sits within the same activity, as do privately managed archives and private library activities.

The code is open across Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales, so its national frame accommodates a wide range of private operators. For PMA, however, Bali is not a matter of selecting a smaller scale or relying on the national ownership ceiling: the record identifies Low and Medium-Low risk across every scope at the Large scale and states that the Bali moratorium blocks all such KBLI for PMA, permanently and island-wide. Founders should therefore read the national position as an ownership rule, and the Bali position as a current registration barrier for foreign investment.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not overcome the Bali-specific block on PMA registration.
